title: Calla's Rainbow Watering Can
markdown:
Calla loved her farm, especially her tall sunflowers, who stood like polite yellow umbrellas along the fence. One morning her favourite blue watering can got a little chip. It made the can look dull, and Calla felt glum. “Oh dear,” she sighed, watering the plants anyway, because sunflowers do not wait for a perfect can. She aimed the hose up and made a fine mist that hung in the warm air like a thousand tiny beads.

Suddenly she gasped. Right where the sunshine hit the water mist, a bright curved arc of colours bloomed: red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, and violet. Tiny water drops sparkled as if they had been keeping a secret and had only just decided to share it.

Sprig the mole popped up from a soft hill of earth, whiskers beaded with the same mist. “What’s that, Calla?”

Dr. Ada, a cloud scientist who happened to be walking the lane with her notebook, noticed too. “Well, I’ll be,” she said, and knelt down so her voice stayed kind and close. “Calla, that white sunlight is actually made of all those colours.” She sprayed the hose again, gently, so the mist did not rush. “These tiny water drops act like little prisms. When sunlight goes through them, it bends and splits into all its colours. Then—poof—a rainbow.”

Calla watched. The water droplets bent the light and spread it out, a quiet unfolding rather than a shout. “It’s like the water is playing with the light?” she wondered.

“Exactly.” Dr. Ada smiled. “The water nudges the sunlight, and all the hidden colours come out to play.”

Calla looked at her chipped watering can. It was not plain at all. She tilted it and made a mist of her own, a smaller softer one that smelled of wet metal and garden. A small rainbow appeared, shy as a first smile. “Wow,” she whispered. Her chipped can was a secret rainbow maker. Happiness fizzed inside her, the kind that makes a dull chip look suddenly important.

“So the water makes the sun colours show up?” Sprig wiggled, earth still on his nose.

“That’s right,” Dr. Ada beamed.

Calla stood a little taller among her sunflowers. Simple things could be spectacular when you understood them. “Even a chipped watering can can make a rainbow,” she said, “if the sun is shining and there are water drops.”

Dr. Ada nodded, already glancing at the next bright patch of sky. “That’s the wonder of science. It shows us amazing things hiding in plain sight. I wonder what other colourful secrets the sun has for us today.”

Calla and Sprig could not wait to find out—especially if the secret needed a little mist, a little chip, and a farm helper who refused to put the watering can away.
characters: Calla (farm helper), Sprig (pop-up mole), Ada (cloud scientist)
author: StoryGen Community
